finding.claim: Hostname suffix check uses a bare endswith('example.com') match, so attacker-owned domains such as evilexample.com pass validation. The server then fetches the attacker-supplied URL, letting the attacker reach internal addresses (e.g. 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1) via DNS pointing at them.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 — query parameter `url` on unauthenticated GET /mirror

trace.note: url: str taken directly from the query string; endpoint has no authentication
if not host.endswith('example.com') -> 400; bare suffix match with no dot boundary or exact match, so 'evilexample.com' passes
c.get(url) fetches the original unvalidated-by-IP URL; the server makes the request
response returned as len(r.text), limiting exfiltration to length but still providing an internal host/port oracle and side-effecting GETs
ALLOWED_SUFFIX = '.example.com' is defined but unused; the intended dot-anchored check was not applied

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check (line 13): insufficient, accepts evilexample.com. Scheme: httpx only supports http/https, so file:/gopher: are effectively blocked. Userinfo (http://example.com@169.254.169.254/) and fragment (#.example.com) tricks: blocked because urlparse returns the real host. Redirects: not a bypass, follow_redirects defaults to False. Resolved-IP check (private/loopback/link-local): absent, this is the gap enabling the DNS bypass. Port restriction: absent. Possible urlparse vs httpx parser differential on edge cases (backslash, unusual authority): unverified, speculative, subsumed by SSRF-1.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is mirror.py:13 `host.endswith("example.com")`, a bare suffix match with no dot boundary or exact-set membership, so it does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is defined but never used. There is no resolved-IP, private-range, or port restriction anywhere in the handler, and the httpx client at mirror.py:15 uses default settings.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated route, the suffix check at mirror.py:13 accepts hosts like evilexample.com, and mirror.py:16 `c.get(url)` makes the server fetch it, so an attacker-owned DNS name resolving to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 reaches internal addresses. All trace lines match the file contents.
